note: The next cycle should keep each active workstream tied to a concrete user behavior: what people understand, trust, find, choose, or feel ready to do next.

comparison_defaults.statement_template: {title} is best treated as a narrowed comparison problem: the next decision should protect the clearest user behavior rather than reopen broad creative exploration.
comparison_defaults.decision_criteria: Choose the strongest direction based on first-glance comprehension, clarity of the next step, user confidence, and whether the page helps visitors complete the intended task.

edc_blueprint_page.finding_statement: Users understand the Enterprise Data Cloud category, but the Blueprint page still needs to make the assessment and workshop outcome clearer before asking visitors to start.
edc_blueprint_page.proof_point: In the 10-second first impression, most respondents called the page "data cloud storage" and fewer than 5 named the Success Blueprint unprompted; half clicked "Start Your Assessment," but expectations were inconsistent and 29% weren't sure it was for them.
edc_blueprint_page.respondent_quote: Why would you assume I'd start an assessment straight away?
edc_blueprint_page.next_step: Clarify what the assessment produces, preview the value of the workshop or output, and validate whether visitors understand why starting the assessment is worth their time.

unresolved.question: Do visitors understand what they get from the assessment and why the workshop is worth engaging with before they have enough context?

accelerate_live_stream.finding_statement: Captured and implemented before launch: first-impression testing drove the deployed live-stream page — a dominant “Watch Live” action and immediate live-state cues, built on the final concept-testing variants. Post-launch, the on-site stream held engagement through both keynotes, peaking at 2,179 concurrent views on Day 1 (June 17) and 683 on Day 2 (June 18).
accelerate_live_stream.proof_point: Pre-launch: fragmented action intent (no dominant CTA), an autoplay mismatch (“Very unclear that this would autoplay”), emotional baseline only “ok.” Post-launch peaks are concurrent, incl. an est. ≥20% internal traffic; net viewership ~2,290 across both days, largely US/UK/Canada.
accelerate_live_stream.respondent_quote: I am not sure if this promotes an event or if it enables me to view it on stream.
accelerate_live_stream.next_step: Reuse the single-dominant-CTA and live-state pattern on future event pages, and instrument on-page “Watch Live” engagement — the stream was ungated, so attribute the page’s role in viewership rather than relying on sign-ups.

unresolved.question: How much of the sustained viewership is attributable to the page experience versus event promotion and the paid simulcast — and does the live-state, single-CTA pattern replicate on the next event page?

contextual_intelligence_pdp.finding_statement: Contextual Intelligence is recognizable as an AI and data management topic, but the differentiation and business value need to become clearer and more operational.
contextual_intelligence_pdp.proof_point: Most visitors grasp the category but miss the differentiation — responses clustered around generic labels ("AI," "data storage"). After a plain-language value statement was added, 66% understood it most or very well; "Watch a Demo" dominated in testing.
contextual_intelligence_pdp.next_step: Translate contextual intelligence into concrete business value and operational trust cues, then validate whether users can explain what makes the capability different.

unresolved.question: Can users explain what contextual intelligence does differently and why that difference matters operationally?

platform_diagram_update.finding_statement: The platform diagram work is really a positioning problem: the story needs to move perception from storage platform to intelligent, AI-ready data platform.
platform_diagram_update.next_step: Simplify the platform diagram around one AI-ready data-platform story and test whether users describe the platform as intelligent and connected rather than only storage-oriented.

unresolved.question: Does the simplified diagram shift perception toward an intelligent AI-ready data platform, or does it still read like a storage architecture diagram?

webinar_landing_page.finding_statement: The webinar experience needs to communicate value faster and make registration feel easier before it can carry more conversion weight.
webinar_landing_page.next_step: Run the next webinar review as a barrier diagnosis: separate value clarity, form effort, session detail, and post-registration expectation so the team knows what is blocking progression.

unresolved.question: Are visitors hesitating because the value of registering is unclear, the form feels too heavy, or the page does not explain what happens after registration?

events_page.finding_statement: Events-page work is pointing toward clearer hierarchy, simpler layouts, and more obvious paths into the full event set.
events_page.next_step: Preserve the simplified hierarchy and clear “Explore All Events” path, then confirm the page still helps visitors find relevant events quickly.

comparison.finding_statement: The Events decision is less about choosing the prettiest layout and more about preserving the behaviors that improved the page: easier scanning, clearer event discovery, and fewer competing visual systems.
comparison.decision_criteria: Pick the winner based on first-glance comprehension, clarity of available events, primary CTA clarity, and whether users know how to move from the page into event detail or registration.
comparison.next_step: Use V4b as the lead direction and evaluate any remaining changes against simplification: fewer competing shapes, clearer featured-event treatment, scannable cards, and no search/CTA pattern that pulls users away from the task they are trying to complete.

comparison.finding_statement: The Homepage AI comparison should protect the balance between AI relevance and human readability. The decision is how much AI language is enough to clarify the offer without making AI itself the object of confusion.
comparison.decision_criteria: Compare versions on comprehension, credibility, relevance, and whether AI language explains a real user benefit without adding abstraction.
comparison.next_step: Compare the next homepage copy against two guardrails: visitors should understand the offer faster, and AI should increase confidence rather than become a vague claim that needs extra explanation.

comparison.finding_statement: The Pathfinder comparison should resolve the tradeoff between recognition and click attraction. “Personalize” explains the outcome better, while start-language creates more entry-point energy.
comparison.decision_criteria: Compare labels on expectation-setting, perceived effort, specificity of the next step, and whether the label reduces hesitation at the point of commitment.
comparison.next_step: Compare a “Personalize” baseline against a start-language hybrid. Pick the label that explains what happens next while still inviting people into the flow.
